passage: Childminder's note, Tuesday afternoon. Baby Chinmay started crying when his rattle rolled away. Thomas, two, who had been busy with blocks, looked over, picked up the rattle, walked across and held it out. He patted Chinmay's head twice. Chinmay stopped crying. I said quietly, "You helped your brother feel better, Thomas," and left it there. Yesterday Thomas would not share his blocks, and I did not bring that up. 🙂

qa.q: What did Thomas do with the rattle?
qa.a: Thomas picked up the rattle, walked across and held it out to Chinmay, then patted his head twice.

qa.q: What might Thomas have been feeling when he saw Chinmay crying?
qa.a: He may have felt concern for his brother, since he stopped his block play, brought the rattle and patted him.

qa.q: Why did the childminder only name the kindness quietly and not ask Thomas to repeat it?
qa.a: Empathy grows better when it is noticed warmly than when it is demanded every time, and Thomas is still very young.

qa.q: How did Chinmay experience the moment?
qa.a: Chinmay was comforted, since his crying stopped once his rattle was back and his brother's hand patted his head.

grounding: Shows an older toddler handing a toy to his crying baby brother and patting him, and a caregiver quietly naming the empathy.
